title: Shivakumar Takes Over as Karnataka CM. Within 48 Hours, a Minister Has Already Quit.
excerpt: DK Shivakumar's swearing-in marks a major Congress transition in Karnataka, but a portfolio dispute has already triggered the first cabinet resignation — testing the new government before it could settle in.
body:
Senior Congress leader DK Shivakumar was sworn in as the 34th Chief Minister of Karnataka on Wednesday in a ceremony at Lok Bhavan in Bengaluru — a political milestone that capped decades of party-building, fundraising, and organisational work in one of Congress's most important states. Within 48 hours, his government faced its first crisis.

Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot administered the oath of office, with Shivakumar holding a copy of the Constitution and invoking the name of revered seer Gangadhar Ajja — a gesture that blended constitutional symbolism with personal faith. G Parameshwara was sworn in as Deputy Chief Minister.

The ceremony drew the Congress party's top leadership: Rahul Gandhi, party president Mallikarjun Kharge, outgoing CM Siddaramaiah, KC Venugopal, Randeep Singh Surjewala, and chief ministers from several Congress-ruled states. Their presence signalled how much the party leadership invested in making the Karnataka transition smooth.

## The Cabinet — and the Crack

On Thursday, Shivakumar allocated portfolios to his 13-member cabinet. He retained Finance, Cabinet Affairs, DPAR, and Intelligence for himself. Deputy CM Parameshwara received Revenue and Sports. Priyank Kharge — seen as a rising Congress strategist — was given Home (excluding Intelligence), IT & BT, and e-Governance.

The allocation triggered an immediate revolt. Senior Congress MLA R Ramalinga Reddy, a veteran Bengaluru politician with 53 years in the party, tendered his resignation just two days after taking oath as minister. His grievance: he was allotted Major and Medium Irrigation instead of the Bengaluru Development portfolio, which he says was promised to him in 2023 as part of a deal that would come into effect once Shivakumar assumed the top post.

"I have been humiliated time and again, cannot take it anymore," Reddy said. He stressed he would remain a Congress MLA and would not leave the party — but could not serve in a cabinet that broke its word.

## Shivakumar's Response

By Saturday, Shivakumar moved to contain the damage. "Under no circumstances will we accept his resignation," he told reporters. He acknowledged receiving Reddy's resignation via WhatsApp but indicated discussions would continue.

"Whatever needs to be done, we will sort it out internally," Shivakumar said — a line calibrated to reassure the party while buying time. The resignation row, coming while Rahul Gandhi was in Bengaluru, added an awkward dimension to what was supposed to be a show of Congress unity.

## What It Means

The leadership change from Siddaramaiah to Shivakumar is the most significant political transition in Karnataka in years. Siddaramaiah's exit was engineered by the Congress high command as part of a pre-agreed power-sharing arrangement — the same arrangement that, according to Reddy, included specific portfolio commitments.

Shivakumar brings a reputation as a ruthless organiser and prolific fundraiser. His elevation is widely seen as a bet on his ability to hold together the party's caste equations and deliver Karnataka in future elections. But the speed of the Reddy crisis exposes a familiar Congress weakness: managing the expectations of its own veterans while trying to project a united front.

For the Indian diaspora watching Karnataka politics — and many NRIs have deep roots in the state — the transition carries weight. Shivakumar's cabinet includes Priyank Kharge in charge of IT and e-Governance, a portfolio that directly affects Bengaluru's tech ecosystem and the thousands of professionals who move between the city and Silicon Valley.

The new government's first real test will not be policy. It will be whether Shivakumar can keep his own team on the field.
